Roleplaying a Dwarven Character
To roleplay a dwarven character, players might emphasize their characterʼs unwavering sense of duty, 
craftsmanship, and pride in their heritage. Heimenhearth dwarves, specifically, will display a strong 
connection to their multiversal home, reflecting a deep reverence for the cosmos and the engineering 
marvels that make their Dyson sphere possible. They will value loyalty and honor, be fiercely protective 
of allies, and take pride in their work. A dwarven character might also have a discerning palate, with a 
love for good ale, hearty food, and celebrations of craft and kinship.
---
Belief System
Dwarven spirituality typically includes gods and deities related to craft, earth, justice, and cosmic order, 
with ancestor worship an essential component. Heimenhearth dwarves take this a step further, with a 
belief system that reveres their ancestors as the “Astral Ancestors,” legendary figures who first 
traversed the multiverse and laid the foundations of Heimenhearth. Rituals involve offerings of rare 
metals or crafted items, given in reverence at forges, celestial observatories, and clan shrines.
Heimenhearthʼs pantheon has adapted to reflect its multiversal reach, with cosmic elements symbolized 
in their deities, and holy places include shrines to the Forge Council, ancient tombs, and stellar forges 
where dwarves pray for protection in the multiverse and the preservation of their people.
---
This reimagined version highlights the dwarves as a widespread race, with Heimenhearth as the most 
multiversally connected dwarven culture. The text incorporates their traditions, physical traits, abilities, 
and multiversal significance, giving them depth and a unique identity within the cosmos.

9. Belief System
Elven spirituality is deeply rooted in reverence for nature, magic, and artistry, with deities and spirits 
that embody these ideals. Sacred groves, arcane temples, and shrines aboard the Etherflotilla reflect 
these beliefs. The Elarian Elves, in particular, revere a pantheon that includes deities of the cosmos and 
travel, given their multiversal journeys. Their rituals often involve the crafting of idols, offerings of rare 
and beautiful items, and ceremonies under starlit skies or in ethereal glades. They strive to maintain 
equilibrium in all things, respecting both the tangible and ethereal aspects of life.
While these traits are generally consistent among elves, individual personalities and subcultures vary 
widely. Some Elarian Elves, especially those raised on different flotilla vessels or with extensive 
exposure to foreign realms, might express more distinct or divergent traits, embodying the adaptability 
and mystery that define their race.
---

The Sharr, being highly rational beings, have a belief system rooted in Empiricism. This is the view that 
knowledge comes primarily from sensory experience. They believe in systematic observation, 
measurement, and experiment, and the formulation, testing, and modification of hypotheses. Their 
"religion" is essentially the pursuit of knowledge and truth. They hold great respect for those who have 
made significant contributions to their understanding of the world, and these individuals are often held 
in high esteem, much like saints or prophets in other cultures. However, they don't deify these figures; 
instead, they see them as models of intellectual pursuit to emulate.

Seasonal Change Mechanism
24-Hour Transition Period: When an Arborae moves from one season to another, either due to 
environmental changes or by entering a new setting (such as moving from a warm, sunlit plain to a cold, 
wintery forest), they begin the transformation process. Over 24 hours, their appearance and abilities 
adjust, allowing their bodies to synchronize with the new season's traits. During this period, they retain 
the previous seasonʼs traits while the new seasonʼs traits start to emerge. The transition concludes at 
the end of this period, at which point the new seasonal traits fully replace the previous ones.
Adaptation to New Settings:
If an Arborae travels to a different climate or setting, they naturally begin shifting to the season most 
reflective of their surroundings. For example:
Moving to a desert might trigger a shift to summer traits.
Entering a lush forest in bloom could initiate the spring traits.
Visiting autumnal woodlands or a harvest season festival might bring out their autumn abilities.
Entering a snowy mountain or winter environment would activate winter traits.
Session-Based Seasonal Triggering:
Within each game session, certain conditions or events can also influence which season is active for an 
Arborae, especially if the Arboraeʼs environment is highly variable or symbolic:
Spring: The appearance of new life, such as blossoming plants or fresh rains, can reinforce spring traits.
Summer: Intense sunlight, high temperatures, or encounters with heat-related events might intensify 
the Arboraeʼs summer traits.
Autumn: Harvest activities, a notable drop in temperature, or the sight of falling leaves could usher in 
autumn traits.
Winter: Cold weather, snow, frost, or moments of dormancy (such as long rest periods) might activate 
winter traits.

🧱  Hardlight Objects
Hardlight items follow these general rules:
• HP = Hit Points, based on item or creature level.
• Hardlight items ignore most poison, disease, and bleed effects.
• Most hardlight lacks mass unless otherwise enhanced (see "Anchored").

Some hardlight is treated as real mass and has momentum (e.g., melee weapons, crashing bridges). Add +1 die 
of damage and apply knockback if used as a weapon or moving object.
🛠  Creating Hardlight Constructs
To create a hardlight item, you must:
1.Have a projector or source (device, spell, creature ability, etc.)
2.Spend an action (unless specified otherwise)
3.Choose a construct type (tool, weapon, structure, etc.)
4.Determine shape and stats based on level, skill, or spell rank

A Tier 2 hardlight projector can generate:
• One Medium weapon (1d8 damage, solid, disappears after 1 minute or on break)
• One 10-ft platform (can hold 500 lbs)
• One basic creature construct (CR 1, controlled by the creator)

energy alignments and devastating breath weapons. Each dragon’s abilities, demeanor, and social ties are 
shaped by its color, forming a complex web of rivalries and alliances.

Elementals can be summoned using magic, advanced tech, or a hybrid system. You must meet the 
following conditions:
•Knowledge Tier: At least Tier 3 in the relevant elementʼs magical, technological, or scientific 
knowledge.
•Skill: Must pass a Conjuring or Engineering skill check (DC 18–25 depending on element and 
strength).
•Medium: A sufficient source of the element must be available (e.g., fire for Fire, a pool for Water).
•Control: Use Command, Control Magic, or a specialized control module to bind the Elemental.
/g0  Binding Elementals
An Elemental will obey for 1 hour per success level (basic success = 1 hour, major success = 3 hours, 
etc.). If your control fails or the bond is broken (e.g., due to damage or disruption), the Elemental 
becomes hostile or flees.
•Rebinding Check: Once control fails, you must succeed a higher DC check (DC +4) to regain control.
⚔  Fighting Elementals: GM Guidelines
Combat Design Tips:
•Elemental Terrain Advantage: Give them terrain that enhances their power (lava pits for Fire, stormy 
skies for Air, caverns for Earth).
•Use Aura and Movement: Let Elementals shape the battlefield through their natural traits.
•Damage Mitigation: Force players to find or create vulnerabilities; raw damage may be ineffective.
•Unusual Behavior: Elementals may not “think” like mortals—make them act with instinct or primal 
patterns, unless directed by a summoner.
Banishing Rules:
•Magic: Banishment spell, exorcism tech, or custom runes can send them away (DC 20+).
•Force: If reduced to 0 HP and their form isn't sustained, they vanish unless anchored.
•Disruption: Removing their elemental source (water drained, fire doused, earth scattered) often 
weakens or banishes them.
🧪  Interacting with Elementals
Elementals can sometimes be reasoned with—especially those born in sentient realities or summoned 
intentionally. Use the following interaction rules:
•Empathy/Persuasion DCs: Start high (DC 25+), reduced if speaking in their tongue or showing 
reverence to their element.
•Trade: Some Elementals may trade resources, knowledge, or assistance for elemental offerings or 
help restoring their realm.
•Taming: Sentient or semi-sentient Elementals may be bound to a pact or contract, functioning 
similarly to mounts, companions, or war machines. Requires custom XP abilities or gear.

Step 3: Assign Ghostly Competencies and Abilities
Ghostly Competencies provide unique actions or abilities to enhance each ghost type, adding depth to 
encounters. Competencies are optional, and you can select or mix and match depending on the spiritʼs 
lore and purpose.
1. Possession: Attempt to possess a creature to control its actions. A successful Charisma save 
prevents possession; the save DC depends on the spiritʼs Charisma modifier.
2. Ethereal Jaunt: Ghosts can freely move between the Ethereal Plane and Material Plane as a bonus 
action, using this ability to avoid attacks or set up ambushes.
3. Haunt Object: Binds to an object, allowing the ghost to manifest around the object or influence 
creatures near it. If destroyed, the ghost is forced to dissipate temporarily.
4. Ghostly Visage: The ghost can show its true, terrifying form, causing creatures within 15 feet to make 
a Wisdom save or be frightened.
5. Soul Drain: Once per day, the spirit can drain 1d8 HP from any creature within 5 feet, using it to 
restore its own health.
6. Curse of Lingering Memory: Ghosts can impose a minor curse on creatures who harm them, causing 
them to suffer nightmares or hallucinations related to the ghostʼs past.

🌿  Mobile
Definition: Mobile plant creatures are fully ambulatory, moving on limbs, tendrils, or root-legs. They act 
like beasts, humanoids, or constructs and may have full combat profiles.
Gameplay Role:
•Serve as traditional combatants—melee or ranged attackers with plant traits.
•May be summoned, tamed, or trained (common in druidic or biotech cultures).
•Can also be intelligent NPCs or sapient symbiotes.
Common Abilities:
•Leaping Roots (jump movement or difficult terrain navigation)
•Thorn Volley (ranged natural weapon)
•Bloomshield (grows a temporary natural shield)
Tactical Note: Often more versatile and unpredictable, especially if intelligent. Best used as party allies, 
elite enemies, or mutated warriors.
🌼  Using Plant Creatures in Gameplay
Encounter Design:
Plant creatures are ideal for:
•Terrain-based puzzles
•Druidic temples or corrupted zones
•Terraforming events or infestations
•Resource harvesting adventures
•Psychic or dreamlike interactions
Harvest Rules (Optional System):
•After defeating a plant creature, players may harvest parts based on survival/nature checks.
•Example:
◦ DC 12: Gather 1 unit of rare wood or petals (value: 20 credits)
◦ DC 16: Harvest alchemical gland or sap (usable in potion crafting)
◦ DC 20+: Obtain a unique crafting reagent, seed, or magical core
Summoning & Grafting:
•Some spells, abilities, or biotech systems allow summoning or fusing with plant creatures.
•Grafted traits might include:

publishedCandidateSample.evidenceText:
---
General Traits of Vampires
- Darkvision: 60 feet (or increases existing Darkvision by 30 feet).  
- Undead Resilience: Resistance to necrotic damage, immunity to poison.  
- Natural Weapons: Gain a bite attack (1d10 piercing damage) with an added effect (see strain-specific 
rules). This attack counts as magical for overcoming resistances.  
- Regeneration: Regain 5 HP at the start of each turn unless damaged by radiant energy or a silver 
weapon in the previous round.  
- Vulnerability to Radiant Damage and Silver: Damage from radiant sources or silver weapons ignores 
resistance and stops regeneration for 1 minute.
---
Unique Strains and Templates  
Players or GMs can select one of the three vampiric strains for further customization. Each strain 
provides a unique set of abilities, drawbacks, and mechanics, along with narrative hooks.
---
Curse-Origin Vampire Template
- Theme: Sophisticated, tragic beings driven by magic and hunger.  
- Weakness: Subject to rules such as requiring permission to enter buildings or being repelled by holy 
symbols.  
- Abilities:  
  - Blood Magic: You can expend HP to cast spells. Each 10 HP spent provides 1 spell level (up to 3rd 
level).  
  - Thrall Creation: When you drain a creature to 0 HP, they rise as a thrall under your control for 24 
hours.  
  - Dominate Person: Use the spell once per long rest. DC 15 Wisdom save.

Weaknesses and Countermeasures

Lycanthropy in Multiversal  
Lycanthropy is a supernatural curse, infection, or blessing that grants individuals animalistic traits, 
enhancing physical abilities at the cost of mental control. The were-creature templates provide unique 
abilities, resistances, and combat advantages in specific situations, creating exciting character and 
narrative opportunities. However, those afflicted with lycanthropy must also face specific drawbacks, 
such as transformations tied to lunar phases or emotional stress, along with vulnerabilities like silver 
weapons.

Core Mechanics of Lycanthropy
1. Transformation Triggers  
   - Full Moon: All were-creatures must transform on the night of a full moon, regardless of location.  
   - Voluntary Transformation: Characters can attempt to shift at will (DC 15 Wisdom save).  
   - Emotional Stress: If the character takes more than half of their max HP in damage or is emotionally 
distressed, they must make a DC 12 Wisdom save. On a failure, they transform involuntarily.  
   - Duration: A transformation lasts for 1 hour or until combat ends, whichever is longer.

◦ Major Traits (Breath weapons, powerful resistances, damage immunities, high CR monster 
abilities): 20,000 - 50,000 XP
8.Custom XP Cost Scaling for Multi-Tiered Abilities
•If the ability improves with CR (e.g., a Minotaurʼs charge deals more damage at higher CR), treat 
it as a multi-tiered ability: 
◦ Basic Version (lowest CR level) = Small XP cost
◦ Advanced Versions (higher CR levels) = Higher XP costs
9.Species Archetype Synergy
•Players who choose a converted species should ensure synergy with their build.
•Some species may benefit from specific skills, attributes, or knowledge, which can be 
suggested by the GM.

52. Engineering
Engineering represents a characterʼs technical expertise in building, repairing, and modifying 
mechanical, electrical, and sometimes even magical devices. This skill covers tasks like fixing damaged 
equipment, constructing useful gadgets, and improving existing technology. Engineering is an essential 
skill for characters who want to maintain gear, design innovative tools, or create custom modifications.
Engineering Skill Checks by DC
DC 10: Performing basic maintenance on simple devices, fixing minor mechanical issues, adjusting 
loose parts.
Example Actions: Tightening bolts on a vehicle, replacing broken components on basic machinery, 
performing routine checks on mechanical systems.
DC 15: Repairing moderate damage to equipment, assembling straightforward gadgets, and diagnosing 
common issues in machinery.
Example Actions: Reconnecting wires in a damaged circuit, reassembling a dismantled clock, fixing 
minor electrical faults.
DC 20: Conducting complex repairs on advanced devices, designing new tools or weapons, and 
optimizing systems for improved performance.
Example Actions: Repairing a damaged engine under time pressure, creating a simple prototype 
weapon, modifying a device to improve efficiency.
DC 25: Crafting intricate machinery, enhancing high-tech or magical equipment, and designing highly 
specialized devices.
